content: Veklury (remdesivir) is indicated for use in patients weighing at least 5 kg who are hospitalized or those who are not hospitalized but have mild-to-moderate COVID-19 and are at high risk of progressing to severe COVID-19, including hospitalization or death. Administration should only occur in a hospital or healthcare setting capable of providing acute care comparable to inpatient hospital care. For children under 12 years of age or weighing less than 40 kg, the dose should be prepared using the lyophilized powder formulation, as per the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for this group. Laboratory tests are recommended, but no dosage adjustment is required for patients aged 65 years or older. Chloroquine reduces the efficacy of remdesivir through an unspecified interaction mechanism. It is advised to avoid or use an alternative drug due to its interference with intracellular metabolic activation and antiviral activity. Similarly, hydroxychloroquine sulfate also decreases the effects of remdesivir via an unspecified interaction mechanism, and its use should be avoided or substituted with an alternative drug. Ublituximab may reduce the effectiveness of remdesivir due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Caution and close monitoring are recommended when these drugs are used together. Remdesivir may enhance the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Available data from clinical trials (e.g., IMPAACT 2032), published reports, the ongoing COVID-PR pregnancy exposure registry, and compassionate use cases in pregnant individuals have not identified any drug-associated risks of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes following exposure during the second and third trimesters. However, there is insufficient data to evaluate the risk of remdesivir exposure during the first trimester. A pharmacokinetic study during pregnancy showed no clinically relevant differences between pregnant and non-pregnant individuals, and no dose adjustments are recommended for pregnant patients receiving this drug. A published case report has documented the presence of remdesivir and its active metabolite GS-441524 in human breast milk. Available pharmacovigilance data do not indicate adverse effects on breastfed infants exposed to remdesivir and its metabolite through breast milk. However, there is no available data on the effects of remdesivir on milk production. For pediatric patients weighing between 5 kg and less than 40 kg, the dose should only be prepared using the lyophilized powder product. The concentrated solution (100 mg/20 mL, or 5 mg/mL) should not be used in pediatric patients under 40 kg or in patients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of less than 30 mL/min due to the higher amount of sulfobutylether-beta-cyclodextrin sodium salt (SBECD) present, which results in higher tonicity compared to the lyophilized powder formulation. Remdesivir should not be administered simultaneously in an intravenous (IV) line with any other medication. The IV infusion should be administered over 30 to 120 minutes. Prescribing information includes infusion rate charts, and the rate of infusion may be adjusted based on the total volume infused. The formulation does not contain preservatives. The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only. Individual treatment plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. For the most current information, contact the applicable plan provider.
